response: Yes, ganglionated plexi ablation during the Maze IV procedure is beneficial for postoperative long-term stable sinus rhythm. This is because ganglionated plexi are clusters of nerve cells that play a role in the regulation of heart rhythm, and ablating them can help to reduce the incidence of atrial fibrillation and promote stable sinus rhythm. Studies have shown that adding ganglionated plexi ablation to the Maze IV procedure can improve long-term outcomes and increase the likelihood of maintaining stable sinus rhythm after surgery.
